why: This gate keeps alternate-runtime support inside explicit v0.10.2 create. Every edit below is a way it could report clean while support widens: a vocabulary waiver applied globally, a support path/rule set grown, a retired asset path ignored, an untracked intended file skipped, a rule disabled, a verdict dropped, a scan shrunk, or an exact exemption allowed to outlive its line.

mutations.name: every rule's pattern stops matching
mutations.breaks: The quiet failure every scanner has: the patterns no longer fire on the thing they name, and every file in the tree reads clean with no symptom at all.
mutations.find:
self.counterexample = counterexample
        # True: refused in every tracked file. False: refused only on the
        # surfaces a reader takes as current.
        self.everywhere = everywhere
mutations.replace:
self.re = re.compile(self.re.pattern + "NEVERMATCHESTHIS")
        self.counterexample = counterexample
        # True: refused in every tracked file. False: refused only on the
        # surfaces a reader takes as current.
        self.everywhere = everywhere

mutations.name: the bare-name rule is applied nowhere
mutations.breaks: The surface rule is skipped for every file, so an unapproved document or source file may claim alternate-runtime support while only harder identifiers remain.
mutations.find:
if not rule.everywhere and not current:
                    continue

mutations.name: the hard rules stop applying off the named surfaces
mutations.breaks: Every rule becomes a current-surface rule, so files outside those prefixes could carry a moving pin, retired asset, or unsupported command untouched.

mutations.name: the workflows drop out of the bare-name rule
mutations.breaks: A workflow is where an installer or unsupported operation comes back. With that directory off current surfaces, a bare alternate-runtime setup claim can pass.
mutations.find: "docs/", ".github/",

mutations.name: a category may be claimed on any path
mutations.breaks: The widest exemption left: an active documentation instruction labelled `negative` keeps its line for ever, because nothing checks that a document cannot make an absence assertion. A category is an argument for keeping a line, and an argument nobody binds to a path is available to every line in the tree.
mutations.find:
wrong = category_problem(entry)
        if wrong:

mutations.name: any file may be declared historical as a whole
mutations.breaks: Whole-file history is the widest exemption in the policy. With the set unpinned, a current document goes back to being declared history in one line — the coordination board's live policy included — and every rule stops applying to it.
mutations.find:
for entry in historical:
        if entry not in HISTORICAL_FILES:
mutations.replace:
for entry in []:
        if entry not in HISTORICAL_FILES:

mutations.name: an exemption matches by substring instead of by exact line
mutations.breaks: An exempted line can be extended with anything at all and keep its exemption: `# the runtime is gone` becomes `# the runtime is gone, install it from here` and stays approved.
mutations.find: hit = exact.get(path, {}).get(stripped)
mutations.replace: hit = next((v for k, v in exact.get(path, {}).items() if k in stripped), None)

mutations.name: a stale exemption is accepted
mutations.breaks: An exemption outlives the line it was written for, so the next person to put residue in that file inherits an approval nobody reviewed.
mutations.find: if id(entry) not in used:

mutations.name: findings are collected and then reported as clean
mutations.breaks: The scan is correct and its verdict is thrown away — indistinguishable from a clean tree from the outside, and the reason the self-test goes through report() and main() rather than only through judge().
mutations.find:
print(f"\n{len(problems)} place(s). Remove the surface, add a legitimate create-support "
              "path to both closed policy sets, or — for an exact refusal, absence assertion, "
              "or explicitly unsupported future — name the line in "
              f"{ALLOWLIST.relative_to(ROOT)} with a category and a reason.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

mutations.name: the floors are computed and ignored
mutations.breaks: An empty enumeration, a scan that read nothing, or a whole directory declared historical all pass. Every one of those looks exactly like success.
mutations.find:
if bad:
        print("check-legacy-runtime: this scan proves nothing", file=sys.stderr)
mutations.replace:
if False:
        print("check-legacy-runtime: this scan proves nothing", file=sys.stderr)

mutations.name: a directory exemption is read as a bare prefix
mutations.breaks: `docs/reviews/` would also cover `docs/reviews-plan.md`, and an entry for `docs/R` would cover `docs/README.md` — an exemption wider than the thing it names.

mutations.name: an empty allowlist is accepted
mutations.breaks: The gate is disabled by emptying its input rather than by editing its code: with no policy loaded, the historical record goes red and somebody deletes the checker instead of the residue.

mutations.name: an exemption needs no category and no reason
mutations.breaks: An approval with nothing written next to it is an approval nobody can review later, which is how an exemption list becomes a way of not fixing things.
mutations.find: if not str(entry.get(field, "")).strip():

mutations.name: an unreadable file is skipped in silence
mutations.breaks: A permissions problem shrinks the scanned set without saying so, and the report still reads clean over the files it managed to open.
mutations.find: findings.append((path, 0, None, f"could not be read (not scanned): {e}"))

mutations.name: the self-exemption set can grow
mutations.breaks: The checker must spell what it forbids, so it skips itself and its allowlist. A third name there is a file that may carry anything, chosen by whoever added it.
mutations.find: if set(SELF) != {"scripts/check-legacy-runtime.py",

mutations.name: the script's entry point is neutered
mutations.breaks: The verdict never reaches an exit code. A self-test that calls the functions directly stays green while the script itself always passes.
mutations.find: sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

mutations.name: scoped vocabulary is waived in every file
mutations.breaks: The central boundary disappears: an unapproved current source file can compose the alternate-runtime create selector and use the API vocabulary merely because those rule classes are scoped somewhere.
mutations.find:
if scoped_rule_allowed(path, rule, line, support):
                    continue

mutations.name: the create selector loses its line-level context check
mutations.breaks: Any bare `--runtime` selection for the alternate runtime is accepted in an approved file, even when it belongs to chat, status, or an unrelated future operation rather than create.
mutations.find:
if rule.name == "create-selector":
        return bool(CREATE_SELECTOR_CONTEXT.search(line))

mutations.name: bounded multiline scanning is disabled
mutations.breaks: An approved support file can split a broad support claim, unsupported command/options source, installer, or retired operation across physical lines and evade every single-line rule.
mutations.find: compound_rules = [rule for rule in RULES if rule.name in MULTILINE_RULES]

mutations.name: multiline compounds ignore syntax connectivity
mutations.breaks: Adjacent but unrelated Markdown table rows or source-list entries are joined into false support claims, making the scoped boundary unusable and hiding whether a real compound was found.
mutations.find: if multiline_lines_are_connected(path, rule, window) and multiline_rule_matches(rule, window):

mutations.name: the multiline window grows beyond its reviewed bound
mutations.breaks: Unrelated source statements or prose can be assembled into one policy finding once the compound scan silently reaches beyond the reviewed four adjacent lines.
mutations.find: MULTILINE_WINDOW_LINES = 4

mutations.name: the code-owned support path set grows
mutations.breaks: A new production file becomes a whole-file vocabulary waiver without being part of the reviewed create implementation. The JSON/code equality alone cannot catch a source edit that grows the authoritative side, so the selftest pins the set independently.
mutations.find:
"cmd/kmx/agent_commands.go",
        "internal/kmx/app/agent_bundle_evaluate.go",

mutations.name: the code-owned support rule set grows
mutations.breaks: Support files begin waiving the retired asset rule, turning the scoped vocabulary boundary into a broad bypass.
mutations.find:
"api-group", "api-kind", "schema-version", "image", "create-selector", "bare-name",
})

mutations.name: retired asset paths are never judged
mutations.breaks: An old installer manifest, CLI package, shim spike, or custom gateway source can return under its retired path even if its contents avoid every literal rule.
mutations.find:
for rule in PATH_RULES:
            if rule.re.search(path):

mutations.name: untracked intended support files are not scanned
mutations.breaks: The normal tree scan uses git by design. Without the direct support-path scan, a new untracked create implementation can carry a moving pin, installer, or retired command until after commit, and mutation verification never proves it.
mutations.find: support_findings, support_read, _ = judge(sorted(support), historical, lines, support)

mutations.name: the workflow support category can spread to another workflow
mutations.breaks: A second workflow could use every scoped alternate-runtime vocabulary class without being part of the reviewed live-create proof.

mutations.name: fixture exemptions can be claimed outside CI
mutations.breaks: The exact official install line could be copied into product code or documentation and retain an installer exemption that was earned only as a disposable-cluster precondition.

mutations.name: arbitrary installer lines can claim the fixture category
mutations.breaks: Any Helm installer in ci.yml could be labelled as a fixture, turning the four-line precondition boundary into a free-form installer allowlist.
mutations.find:
if entry["text"].strip() not in FIXTURE_LINES:
            return "only the four closed official chart pull/install lines are runtime fixtures"
mutations.replace:
if False:
            return "only the four closed official chart pull/install lines are runtime fixtures"

mutations.name: the closed fixture line set grows
mutations.breaks: A fifth chart-operation spelling could become an exact exemption without the selftest noticing that the reviewed four-line boundary widened.
mutations.find: FIXTURE_LINES = frozenset({CRDS_PULL_LINE, CHART_PULL_LINE, CRDS_FIXTURE_LINE, CHART_FIXTURE_LINE})
mutations.replace: FIXTURE_LINES = frozenset({CRDS_PULL_LINE, CHART_PULL_LINE, CRDS_FIXTURE_LINE, CHART_FIXTURE_LINE, f"helm install extra {NAME}"})

mutations.name: the closed fixture line set loses a reviewed command
mutations.breaks: Removing one official precondition from the code-owned set would make the policy data impossible to load; the mutation proves that shrinkage cannot be mistaken for a clean scan.
mutations.find: FIXTURE_LINES = frozenset({CRDS_PULL_LINE, CHART_PULL_LINE, CRDS_FIXTURE_LINE, CHART_FIXTURE_LINE})

mutations.name: the closed workflow support set drops CI
mutations.breaks: Removing the live proof workflow from the code-owned support set must fail against the independently pinned JSON boundary rather than silently stop scanning its supported vocabulary.

mutations.name: fixture lines waive an unsupported operation rule
mutations.breaks: Even an exact external precondition line may waive only the installer and retired-asset findings it necessarily carries; adding an operation rule would make the category broader than its argument.
mutations.find: FIXTURE_RULES = frozenset({"installer", "asset"})

mutations.name: negative controls waive broader operations
mutations.breaks: An exact CI or test assertion may exercise retired syntax, but it must not become an escape hatch for a future version or newly supported lifecycle operation.

mutations.name: kubectl manifest installs are ignored
mutations.breaks: A scoped documentation or workflow file could apply an alternate-runtime release manifest while the waived bare-name and image rules make that installer invisible.
mutations.find:
r"(?i:\bkubectl\b.{0,120}\b(?:apply|create|replace)\b.{0,80}"
          r"(?:-f|--filename|-k|--kustomize)(?:=|\s+)\S*" + NAME + r")|"
